analogs.covers: How it hunts: a silent night stalk that ends in a leap onto prey bigger than itself
How it lives: a long-legged nocturnal nomad bonded to one partner for life

headline: A night-hunting caracal that lives as a lifelong maned-wolf pair and hunts big game with its rook-like Latenivenatrix partners.

setting.label: Night roamer of woods, hills and wetland edges
setting.note: Nomadic and strictly nocturnal for hunting. Holds no big territory of its own; only the small nest territory it shares with its bonded Latenivenatrix rookery.

playsLike: You are a quiet, medium-sized night stalker with long legs and sickle claws, living in a lifelong pair. Alone or as a pair you creep up and take prey up to Large tier. With three bonded Latenivenatrix at your side you can bring down solo Apex animals. You avoid Apex carnivore pairs and may not scavenge, so every meal is earned by stalking.

why.text: Moves quietly, stalks close without being detected and prefers larger targets it cuts with sickle talons. That is the caracal's silent approach and its leap onto prey bigger than itself (official inspiration).

Up to 2 sub/adults with pairbonds that often become lifelong and are 'a core part of their survival into adulthood'. Maned wolves live as monogamous pairs that share one territory for life (official inspiration).
Nocturnal hunter that may do everything except hunting by day, like both the caracal and the maned wolf.
Medium tier, 2,800 combat weight, sprint 1,050 held for a long 154 s. A mid-sized predator that must pick its fights: up to Large alone, Apex only with 3 Latenivenatrix, and never Apex pairs.

It flushes small prey into dens for Latenivenatrix, which drive it back out. Coyotes and badgers use the same trick together. On big game the Latenivenatrix leap onto the flanks, much like ravens working alongside a wolf hunt.

notLike: Caracals are solitary; Achillobator is built around its mate.
Maned wolves eat mostly fruit and small animals; Achillobator is a pure carnivore that targets Iguanodon, Parasaurolophus or Eotriceratops when its partners are along.
